name: Triacetyldiphenolisatin

own_problems.text: Pulled from the market in Australia and 3 other countries, first in 1971 — for liver harm

similar.name: Oxyphenisatin Acetate
problems: Pulled from the market in United States and 18 other countries, first in 1970 — for liver harm

similar.name: Cyclofenil
problems: Pulled from the market in France, first in 1987 — for liver harm

summary: Triacetyldiphenolisatin was pulled from the market in Australia and three other countries starting in 1971 due to liver harm [3]. A small computer model, rather than tests on people, gave the drug a medium risk score of 58 for the liver and a low risk score of 29 for the heart [M]. Additionally, two similar drugs named Oxyphenisatin Acetate and Cyclofenil were also removed from markets in countries including the United States and France because of liver harm [4][5].
